summary: KGP / JS: allow relative paths when declaring local npm dependencies
description:
Currently, declaring a local npm dependency is possible by using the `file` protocol:

```
implementation(npm(file(localNpmPackageDir)))
```

However, internally KGP always [converts](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin/blob/71770ee51423d1f34cee14aa5e04bb83c053f3b0/libraries/tools/kotlin-gradle-plugin/src/common/kotlin/org/jetbrains/kotlin/gradle/targets/js/npm/NpmDependency.kt#L83) the file's path to an absolute one.

To allow using local packages in shared environments (e.g. CI) KGP should not try to always do the conversion, but instead:

1. if the file's path is absolute, do nothing
2. if the file's path is relative, adjust it to take into account the generated `package.json` location under `build/js/<module>/`

Also see Slack [discussion](https://kotlinlang.slack.com/archives/C0B8L3U69/p1736247633554919).

### Steps to reproduce

1. With a KGP/JS project set `kotlin.js.yarn=false` to use npm.
2. Create a local npm package in the project, `$projectDir/local-lib`.
3. Depend on it:

   ```kotlin
   kotlin {
       js { browser() }
       sourceSets {
           jsMain.dependencies {
               implementation(npm(project.file("local-lib")))
           }
       }
   }
   ```

5. Run `./gradlew kotlinUpgradePackageLock`
6. Check kotlin-js-store/package-lock.json. It contains the absolute path:

   ```json
   "local-lib": "file:/Users/me/repro/local-lib"
   ```
7. Copy or clone the project to a different directory and run `./gradlew build` there
8. `kotlinStorePackageLock` fails with "Lock file was changed. Run the kotlinUpgradePackageLock task to actualize lock file"

With `kotlin.js.yarn=true` the same steps pass, because `yarn.lock` has no entry for the local package.
